transcript: Speaker A: Hello, what is your name? [Hello, what is your name?] Speaker B: My name is Zara. [My name is Zara.] Speaker A: Zara, tell me about your family. [Zara, tell me about your family.] Speaker B: I am having one brother and one sister. [I am having one brother and one sister.] Speaker A: I am having nahi, I have one brother and one sister hota hai. Having tab lagate hain, jab kuch abhi ho raha ho. Jaise I am having tea. Brother tea nahi hai, jo abhi ho raha hai. [It's not 'I am having', it is 'I have one brother and one sister'. 'Having' is used when something is happening right now. Like 'I am having tea'. A brother is not tea that is happening right now.] Speaker B: Okay, okay. I have one brother and one sister. [Okay, okay. I have one brother and one sister.] Speaker A: Good. Ab batao, kal kya kiya tumne? [Good. Now tell me, what did you do yesterday?] Speaker B: Yesterday I didn't went to college. [Yesterday I didn't went to college.] Speaker A: Didn't went nahi hota, didn't go hota hai. Jab didn't laga diya, toh baad mein simple form aayega. Go, eat, sleep. Didn't went matlab tumne past tense do baar laga diya. [It's not 'didn't went', it is 'didn't go'. When you use 'didn't', the simple form follows. Go, eat, sleep. 'Didn't went' means you used the past tense twice.] Speaker B: Are yaar, ye toh basic hai aur mujhe ye bhi nahi aata. Class mein sab English mein baat karte hain, main chup rehti hoon. [Oh man, this is basic and I don't even know this. Everyone speaks in English in class, I stay quiet.] Speaker A: Chup isliye rehti ho kyunki darr lagta hai, galat bol dogi toh koi hasega, hai na? [You stay quiet because you are afraid that if you speak incorrectly, someone will laugh, right?] Speaker B: Haan, ek baar canteen mein friend ne pucha, 'What did you eat?' Maine bola, 'I eated rice.' Sab hase. Tab se muh nahi kholti. [Yes, once in the canteen a friend asked, 'What did you eat?' I said, 'I eated rice.' Everyone laughed. Since then, I don't open my mouth.] Speaker A: Eated nahi hota, I ate rice hota hai. Eat ka past tense ate hai, irregular verb hai. Par tumhari galti nahi hai. Tumse 500 baar galti karwaungi, har baar sudharungi. Kabhi nahi bolungi, 'itna bhi nahi aata'. [It's not 'eated', it is 'I ate rice'. The past tense of 'eat' is 'ate', it's an irregular verb. But it's not your fault. In school, they made you memorize rules, they didn't explain them. That's why the English Seekho app was made. There are short videos by experts, explaining in Hindi.
